findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:117,341,1105,1403 — `agyPrintTimeout` is unreachable dead plumbing in the new managed run spec. This story removed `agy` from the managed `host_run` surface (`normalizeHost` in handlers/host-run.ts now rejects it, and the `--agyPrintTimeout` CLI flag was deleted from command-catalog.ts), yet `ManagedHostRunSubmitArgs.agyPrintTimeout`, the persisted `ManagedHostRunSpec.agyPrintTimeout` field, and the forwarding at submit/worker time were all retained. No production caller can set it: `host_run` no longer accepts the flag, and cross-host-review only submits `host: 'codex'`. The field is therefore permanently null on every managed run, and it is serialized into the immutable, digest-sealed spec.json for every run. Maintainability only — it cannot change behavior. (Note: the separate `host-run.ts` / `host-execution-readiness.ts` uses of the same name remain live for non-managed readiness probes and are correctly retained.)

packages/main/src/core/managed-review-evidence.ts:185 — `catch (error)` binds `error` but never reads it. The catch wraps the three artifact loads (managedHostRunReceipt / readManagedReviewEvidenceProposal / readManagedHostRunBinding) and discards the concrete failure, substituting a generic `failedDiagnostic()` whose every check field is hardcoded false. An operator debugging a rejected import therefore cannot distinguish a missing terminal receipt from a corrupt proposal from an unreadable run binding — all three collapse to the same all-false diagnostic. Severity is low, not higher, because I verified the shared Proof Admissibility evaluator still emits canonical registered reason codes and remediation text (proof-admissibility-gates.ts:150-158), so the checklist's 'specific remediation' promise is not broken; only the underlying cause is lost.
